title: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus) Bill 2020
short_title: Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus) Bill 2020

summary.attribution: Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
sentences: The bill would amend social services offences and confidentiality rules, allowing Royal Commissions to compel protected information while removing obsolete provisions and correcting legislative errors.
Existing offences involving reckless false or misleading statements would extend to submissions assessed automatically by Services Australia, without communication to an individual officer.

Compelled disclosures would retain reasonable-excuse protections, including legal professional privilege and public interest immunity, with technical amendments commencing in stages alongside earlier welfare reforms.
changes: Covered secrecy provisions would no longer prevent compliance with Royal Commission notices or summonses.
Obsolete Mature Age Allowance and Mature Age Partner Allowance provisions would be removed.
Provisions for one-off payments to older Australians in 2006, 2007 and 2008 would be repealed.
summary.affected: Social security claimants, Services Australia and departmental officers, Royal Commissions and people whose protected information is sought are affected.

speeches.speaker: Stuart Robert
speeches.brief: The Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus) Bill 2020 compels the Department of Social Services and Services Australia to comply with royal commission compulsory notices for information under secrecy provisions, and clarifies that reckless false-document and false-statement offences apply when Services Australia uses automated processes. The bill also removes obsolete provisions, corrects errors, and updates legislation to improve accessibility and policy delivery.

speeches.speaker: Vince Connelly
speeches.brief: The speaker supported the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus) Bill 2020, arguing it enables technical amendments for smoother delivery of social services. He noted the government's extension of JobSeeker payments to March next year and shared his personal experience of briefly relying on unemployment benefits after leaving the Army, encouraging Australians not to feel guilty about using the safety net while aiming to return to work.

speeches.speaker: Luke Howarth
speeches.brief: The Morrison government introduced the Social Services and Other Legislation Amendment (Omnibus) Bill 2020, which makes technical and administrative amendments to social services law, including allowing royal commission notices to override portfolio secrecy provisions, updating offence provisions for automated claims processing, and removing obsolete provisions. The government also reaffirmed its commitment to social security, citing JobKeeper, JobSeeker and other coronavirus stimulus measures as beneficial.
